title: A storage interface in front of the three stores
request: The product moves to PostgreSQL for one team of about 1,000 users. First put one small interface in front of the project, draft and intern-session stores, with today's files as the first implementation, and change no behaviour.
spec: A Protocol each for projects, drafts and intern sessions in dclab_rnd/storage/, with exactly the methods callers use today (get, save, update under a lock, list, delete, the append-only logs, the data folder); the file stores implement them and every caller depends on the Protocol. Done when every route and module reaches storage only through the interface and make rd-check and make product-e2e pass unchanged.
plan: List the methods of ProjectStore, DraftStore and SessionStore and count every attribute use outside the stores (store.home, data_dir, directory, path, private locks).
Find the callers that build paths inside a store's folder: the agent's turn lock, the Admin page, the Compute page twice, the intern's export.
Write dclab_rnd/storage/__init__.py with one Protocol per store stating the whole surface callers may use.
Add the missing methods to the file stores (an export folder, the draft's pipeline events, the turn lock) and move the five callers onto them.
Write a test that fails when a store drifts from its Protocol or when code outside the stores reaches into their folders again.
Run make rd-check and make product-e2e; commit.

decisions.decision: The Protocols hold exactly what callers use today, nothing more.
decisions.why: A wider interface would have to be built twice in 9.2 for no caller; a narrower one would leave callers reaching into folders.

decisions.decision: Give the stores methods for the five folder-reaching uses instead of exposing paths.
decisions.why: A path inside a store's folder means nothing once the store is a database; a method can be implemented by either backend.

decisions.decision: Guard the boundary with a test, not a convention.
decisions.why: The next change that reaches into a store's folder would break PostgreSQL mode silently; a test that greps for it fails at once.

change: New dclab_rnd/storage/__init__.py with Projects, Drafts and Sessions Protocols. studio/store.py and draft/store.py gained the methods the folder-reaching callers needed (export folder, pipeline events, turn lock). agentic/pages/ops.py, agentic/pages/platform.py, draft/chat.py and intern/tools.py now call those methods. tests/test_storage_interface.py checks each file store against its Protocol and refuses folder access outside the stores.

findings.defect: Five callers built paths inside a store's folder and would break as soon as storage stops being files.
findings.scenario: The Home agent's turn lock, the Admin page, the Compute page (twice) and the intern's notebook export each joined store.home or data_dir with a file name; with a database behind the store there is no such folder, so each would fail or read nothing.
findings.cause: The stores had no method for these uses, so callers reached around them.
findings.fix: Each use became a store method; the callers call it.
findings.test: tests/test_storage_interface.py: code outside the stores that reaches into their folders fails the test.

outcome: Done: one interface in front of the three stores, the five folder-reaching callers moved onto it, behaviour unchanged; make rd-check passed (320 tests) and make product-e2e passed all four flows.
lessons: Before replacing a storage backend, count every use of the old one's internals outside it; those are the places a new backend breaks.
A refactor meant to change nothing is proven by the existing suite and end-to-end flows passing without edits to their expectations.
